correctness.rationale: Incrementing n flips exactly ν₂(n+1) trailing ones to zeros and one zero to one, yielding the given first-difference congruence. Every length-three window has one difference 1 because among its two transition indices one is odd. For its reverse to occur it must also have a difference −1; since 1 and −1 are distinct modulo every ℓ≥3, the two differences sum to zero and the original factor is a palindrome. At length four the two parity cases exhaust all windows. When the two outer transition indices are odd, the triple is (1,a,1); otherwise the middle difference is 1 and exactly one even outer transition index is 2 mod 4, guaranteeing an outer zero. Negative reversal of (1,a,1) has neither two outer ones nor an outer zero; negative reversal of the other pattern has middle −1 and an outer zero. Both are excluded from both types. Taking the length-four prefix and the corresponding suffix of the reversal proves the assertion for all longer factors, including the palindrome exclusion. The equivalence classes of factors therefore have no mergers at lengths ≥3. Separately, the replay used the substitution x↦x(x+1) modulo ℓ. For k=12 every output window of length ≤k comes from a parent window of length ≤k, so iterating the bounded factor-set map from 0 to a fixed point gives the exact languages up to that length. It confirmed both claims for ℓ=3,…,9 and the recorded six modulus-four pairs. The proof, not that bounded check, covers every ℓ and length.
residual_risks: The replay settles only the listed finite lengths and moduli; the general result is established by symbolic parity and difference arguments.
